items: Secure Digital Evidence: Export and screenshot all relevant company emails before access is revoked, including sent messages, performance discussions, and termination-related communications.
Secure Digital Evidence: Screenshot every relevant conversation from Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat that shows your performance, complaints filed, or discussions about termination decisions.
Secure Digital Evidence: Use your phone camera to photograph your screen as a backup, since physical photographs are harder for employers to claim were digitally altered or manipulated.
Secure Digital Evidence: Preserve metadata by capturing document properties including author, creation date, and edit history to reveal inconsistencies in your employer's stated timeline.
Compile Employment Records: Export all performance reviews, goal sheets, and feedback from Workday, BambooHR, or Lattice before your system access is completely revoked.
Compile Employment Records: Screenshot all internal HR complaints you filed, including the original complaint, every response received, and any follow-up messages marked as resolved.

Compile Employment Records: Photograph your termination letter and capture its metadata properties, since a letter created on your termination date tells a very different story than one modified in advance.
Compile Employment Records: Document any evidence deletion attempts by screenshotting access warnings, disappearing messages, or bounced emails that indicate your employer is destroying records.

File Administrative Complaints: File your complaint with the EEOC or state fair employment agency within the required timeframe, since statutes of limitation are strict and missing the deadline bars your entire case.
File Administrative Complaints: Request a Right to Sue letter from the EEOC if you need to pursue a civil claim, as this step is typically required before you can file a lawsuit in federal court.

File Administrative Complaints: Submit your complaint to both the EEOC and your state agency if your state has separate jurisdiction, because dual filing strengthens your case and expands potential remedies.

File Administrative Complaints: Keep copies of every complaint you file and document the date, confirmation number, and method of delivery, since proof of timely filing is essential if your case is challenged.
